purpose: Rabeprazole is used to reduce the amount of acid your stomach makes. It helps treat conditions like heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), stomach ulcers, and a condition called Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It can also be used as part of a treatment plan to get rid of a stomach bacteria called H. pylori.
how_it_works: Your stomach has tiny pumps that produce acid to help digest food. Rabeprazole works by blocking these pumps so they make much less acid. With less acid in your stomach, your symptoms like heartburn and pain can heal and feel better over time.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication well, but some may notice headache, diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain, or gas. You might also feel a little constipated or get a runny nose. These side effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: If you take this medicine for a long time, it can lower your magnesium and vitamin B12 levels, so your doctor may check these with blood tests. Long-term use has also been linked to a slightly higher risk of bone fractures and a gut infection called C. difficile. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, are pregnant, breastfeeding, or take blood thinners like warfarin or clopidogrel, as rabeprazole can interact with these.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 20 mg taken once a day, typically before a meal — often in the morning. Your doctor may adjust the dose depending on your condition. Always swallow the tablet whole and do not crush or chew it. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, even if you start feeling better.
